questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{y}-z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,e).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }k \\  & ={e}^{y}\text{ }i+x{e}^{y}\text{ }j-k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,e) & ={e}^{1}\text{ }i+(1){e}^{1}\text{ }j-k \\  & =e\,i+e\,j-k \\  & =⟨e,e,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,e)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-e⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨e,e,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-e⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${x}^{2}=-xyz.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(4,2,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =-xyz \\ {x}^{2}+xyz & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+xyz$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

 

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(4,2,-2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }k \\  & =(2x+yz)\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(4,2,-2) & =(2(4)+2(-2))\text{ }i+4(-2)\text{ }j+4(2)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i-8j+8\,k \\  & =⟨4,-8,8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(4,2,-2)\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-2,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,-8,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-2,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-4)+(-8)(y-2)+8(z+2) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+8z+16 & =0 \\ x-2y+2z+4=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-y{e}^{z}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-y{e}^{z})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-y{e}^{z})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x-y{e}^{z}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{2}{x}\text{ }i-{e}^{z}\text{ }j-y{e}^{z}k \\ ∇\,f(1,2,1) & =\frac{2}{1}\text{ }i-{e}^{1}\text{ }j-(2){e}^{1}k \\  & =2\,i-e\,j-2ek \\  & =⟨2,-e,-2e⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,2,1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-e,-2e⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=6{x}^{2}-y+{z}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(\frac{1}{2},3,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(\frac{1}{2},3,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(6{x}^{2}-y+{z}^{3})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(6{x}^{2}-y+{z}^{3})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(6{x}^{2}-y+{z}^{3})\text{ }k \\  & =12x\text{ }i-\text{ }j+3{z}^{2}k \\ ∇\,f(\frac{1}{2},3,2) & =12\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{ }i-\text{ }j+3(2)^{2}k \\  & =6\,i-\,j+12k \\  & =⟨6,-1,12⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(\frac{1}{2},3,2)\cdot ⟨x-\frac{1}{2},\,y-3,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨6,-1,12⟩\cdot ⟨x-\frac{1}{2},\,y-3,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 6(x-\frac{1}{2})-(y-3)+12(z-2) & =0 \\ 6x-y+12z-24 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $xy{z}^{2}=6-z.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}xy{z}^{2} & =6-z \\ xy{z}^{2}+z & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=xy{z}^{2}+z$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=6.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }k \\  & =(y{z}^{2})\text{ }i+(x{z}^{2})\text{ }j+(2xyz+1)\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,2) & =(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }i+(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }j+(2(1)(1)(2)+1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i+4j+5\,k \\  & =⟨4,4,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,4,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-1)+4(y-1)+5(z-2) & =0 \\ 4x+4y+5z-18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
